## Big idea in one line

**A transaction is one business unit of work.**  
All steps succeed together, or none stick. Spring’s `@Transactional` marks that boundary so you do not hand-write begin/commit/rollback every time.

```text
Transfer ₹1000 A → B
  UPDATE A  -1000
  UPDATE B  +1000
Must be ONE transaction (not half a transfer)
```

---

## Topic 1 — ACID (plain)

| Letter | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **A** Atomicity | All or nothing |
| **C** Consistency | Valid state → valid state (rules/constraints hold) |
| **I** Isolation | Concurrent TXs do not corrupt each other carelessly |
| **D** Durability | After commit, result survives crash |

Isolation details deepen in lecture 34.

---

## Topic 2 — Begin / commit / rollback

```text
BEGIN  → work → COMMIT   (keep changes)
BEGIN  → work → ROLLBACK (discard uncommitted work)
```

JDBC picture:

```java
connection.setAutoCommit(false);
// SQL...
connection.commit();   // or rollback()
```

Spring picture:

```java
@Transactional
public void transfer(Long fromId, Long toId, BigDecimal amount) {
    debit(fromId, amount);
    credit(toId, amount);
}
```

```text
proxy begins TX
  → method body
  → success → commit
  → rollback-eligible exception → rollback
```

---

## Topic 3 — Layers (same DB TX, different APIs)

```text
@Service @Transactional
        │
        ▼
 Spring transaction manager
        │
        ▼
 JPA EntityManager / Hibernate Session
        │
        ▼
 JDBC Connection
        │
        ▼
 Database transaction
```

You are not choosing “Spring TX **or** DB TX.” Spring **coordinates** the lower APIs.

---

## Topic 4 — Where to put `@Transactional`

Prefer **service layer** (one use case = one boundary).

```java
@Service
public class AccountService {

    @Transactional
    public void transfer(Long fromId, Long toId, BigDecimal amount) {
        // several repository calls
    }

    @Transactional(readOnly = true)
    public Account get(Long id) {
        return accounts.findById(id).orElseThrow();
    }
}
```

Class-level `@Transactional` sets a default; method-level can override.

### Rollback rules (default mental model)

| Exception type | Default |
|----------------|---------|
| Runtime exception / Error | **Rollback** |
| Checked exception | **Commit** (unless configured) |

Override with `rollbackFor` / `noRollbackFor` when needed (more in lecture 34 attributes).

---

## Topic 5 — Proxy reminder

`@Transactional` works through a Spring **proxy**.

```text
OtherBean → accountService.transfer()  ✓ goes through proxy
accountService.internal() calling this.transfer()  ✗ may skip proxy
```

Call transactional methods from **another bean**, or redesign so the boundary is the outer public method.

## Practice lab

1. Two accounts with balances.  
2. `transfer` debits then credits inside `@Transactional`.  
3. Throw a `RuntimeException` after debit; confirm both balances unchanged.  
4. Remove `@Transactional`; observe partial update risk.  
5. Mark a read method `readOnly = true`.  
6. Log SQL; confirm writes share one transactional unit.

---

## Short map to keep

```text
Business use case
   └─ @Transactional on service
         begin → repos/EM work → commit | rollback
ACID = why we bother
```
